quote: whose name Dante has celebrated in the tenth canto

text: Lucullus, a Roman general famous for luxury, scolded his cook for serving a plain meal when he dined alone: 'Lucullus dines with Lucullus tonight.' The Count means the dinner must be splendid whoever comes.
quote: ‘Lucullus dines with Lucullus,’ that is quite sufficient

text: A long, close-fitting man's overcoat. The 'frogs' are the ornamental braid fastenings across the front, a military look that was decades out of date in 1838 Paris.
quote: dressed in one of the green surtouts

text: A small city-state in Tuscany, in 1838 still an independent duchy. Its old families claimed proud descent, which makes it a handy birthplace for an invented nobleman.
quote: a worthy patrician of Lucca

text: After 1815 Austria ruled Lombardy and Venetia and dominated the rest of Italy, so many Italians served in its army. The French rather looked down on Austrian officers, as the count jokes.
quote: Ex-major in the Austrian service?

text: A sweet, dark Spanish dessert wine from the region of Alicante, often taken with a biscuit.
quote: Alicante, if you please; it is my favorite wine.

text: Italian: 'By Bacchus!' (a mild oath) and 'Oh, what a pity!'
quote: Ah, _perbacco_, indispensable, were they?

term: Marriage is a civil affair in France
text: Since the Revolution a French marriage has been legally valid only when performed by a civil official (the mayor), backed by birth and identity papers. A church wedding alone counted for nothing in law.
quote: Marriage is a civil affair in France

quote: credit on you for the further sum of 48,000 francs

text: Medals and badges of chivalric orders, worn on the coat on formal occasions. France had mocked such decorations since the Revolution yet still prized them, as the count says.
quote: Do not forget your crosses.

quote: inscribed in the golden book at Florence

text: A town on the frontier between France and Savoy, which then belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia. Crossing there meant entering France from Italy.
quote: from Pont-de-Beauvoisin to Paris

quote: the slaves were treated in Asia Minor

quote: man proposes, and God disposes

quote: he said, in very excellent Tuscan

text: A light, fast, open four-wheeled carriage with large wheels, driven by its owner: the sports car of a fashionable young man.
quote: if you purchase a phaeton

text: Full evening dress for a formal dinner: an officer wore uniform and decorations; civilians of the old school still wore knee-breeches rather than trousers.
quote: uniform, cross, knee-breeches

text: Lucerne is alfalfa, a clover-like fodder crop. The chapter title refers to the field of it outside the Villefort garden, where Maximilian waits by the gate.

quote: Now, if I had taken the veil

text: A legal term: property that passes to someone after another person's interest in it ends. Here the money would go first to Villefort, then on to Edward.
quote: and, in reversion, to his son

term: sabring right and left among the Bedouins

quote: sabring right and left among the Bedouins

quote: they told me it was 4,500 francs

text: A light two-wheeled, one-horse carriage with a folding hood: the Paris cab of the day (and the origin of the word 'cab').
quote: so I took a cabriolet

quote: He was placed before a large glass

quote: took their places on either side of the paralytic

text: French: boredom, weariness. Villefort could talk with his father through the eye signals but rarely bothers to.
quote: indifference and _ennui_ which prevented him

quote: provided it be read in the presence of seven witnesses

quote: You are then in possession of 900,000 francs?

quote: found 900,000 francs in bank scrip

quote: your residuary legatee?

quote: the law does not allow a son to be entirely deprived

quote: the terrible theories of The Mountain

term: the senator's robe, which Napoleon cast on his shoulders

quote: the senator’s robe, which Napoleon cast on his shoulders

text: Brother of Louis XVIII and King of France from 1824 until the July Revolution of 1830 drove him out. He made many royalist creations of nobility.
quote: created Baron d’Épinay by Charles X.

quote: its black arms, bending in every direction

quote: a sign from M. Duchâtel, or from M. Montalivet

text: Greek: 'far' and 'to write'. Together they make 'telegraph', far-writing.
quote: two Greek words, _têle_, _graphein_

quote: the Barrière d’Enfer, taking the road to

quote: reached the tower of Montlhéry

quote: I have read so in Petronius

quote: Next morning _Le Moniteur_ contained the following

quote: The funds rose one per cent higher

text: From Fénelon’s hugely popular novel Télémaque (1699), in which the nymph Calypso welcomes the shipwrecked son of Ulysses ashore and offers him fresh clothes.
quote: as Calypso said to Telemachus

term: He who is about to die salutes you
text: The Latin Morituri te salutant, which the Roman historian Suetonius reports men condemned to fight said to the Emperor Claudius.
quote: ‘He who is about to die salutes you.’

term: the ancient Romans condemned by Nero
text: Nero often ordered out-of-favour Romans to kill themselves. Some, like the writer Petronius, made a graceful show of it, opening their veins at a banquet among friends.
quote: those ancient Romans, who when condemned by Nero

quote: similar to the Caryatides
